## Chapter Summary

Data preparation transforms data from the form in which it was recorded into the form an analysis needs. In accounting, it usually means bringing attributes that live in related tables onto the transactions being analyzed. A preparation error changes every number that follows without announcing itself. Every preparation step should therefore be paired with a check, such as a count of unmatched rows or a total that must agree with its source, and the whole procedure should be documented so that someone else can repeat it.

Text functions extract, standardize, and validate text fields. MID, LEFT, RIGHT, FIND, and LEN extract the parts of a structured value, such as the product type in a Charles River item code. TRIM, CLEAN, SUBSTITUTE, UPPER, LOWER, and PROPER standardize text. Apply them only after a test shows that a field needs them, because standardizing clean data can damage it, as PROPER does to a name such as Donaldson LLC. Date functions assign transactions to fiscal periods and measure the time between events. A non-calendar fiscal year needs an adjusted quarter formula, and a fixed as-of date is more reliable than TODAY for any measure of age.

Logical functions classify and test values. IF returns one of two values depending on a test, IFS returns the value for the first of several tests that is true, and AND, OR, and NOT combine tests. IFERROR substitutes a value when a formula returns an error, which is useful when the substitute can be counted, such as "No match".

Lookup functions retrieve a value from one table using a key from another. XLOOKUP is the most flexible, INDEX and MATCH work in every version of Excel, and VLOOKUP is limited to keys in the first column. A lookup is correct when it follows a relationship toward its "one" side. Toward the "many" side it returns only the first match, and MINIFS, SUMIFS, and COUNTIFS are the right tools. Counting the rows a lookup failed to match is the first check on any lookup. Preparation also separates blanks that record a fact, such as a missing PromotionID on a line with no promotion, from blanks that mean information is missing. It also checks that values are valid for their purpose, which the fractional quantities on items sold by the unit are not.

Power Query performs the same preparation as a recorded, refreshable procedure. A merge combines two queries on a key column, and its join kind, usually left outer, decides which rows appear. Custom columns calculate new values with Power Query's formula language. Applied to the Charles River data, these tools produced InvoiceLines, a single table in which every invoice line carries its fiscal period, product group and type, and customer segment. Its totals agree with the source and with the lookups. Preparing it also showed that many lines of the Furniture Seasonal Promotion were invoiced after the promotion ended.
